met_analysis:
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level passes through Firozpur, Ambala, Bareilly, Gorakhpur, Purnea and thence eastwards to Manipur.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 72°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northwest Bihar & neighbourhood now lies over Northeast Bihar & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over South Bangladesh & neighbourhood at 5.8 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level.
A trough runs from North Bangladesh to North Bay of Bengal and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Bangladesh & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The trough in westerlies along Long. 87°E to the north of Lat. 24°N between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
